polity.canonical_name_en: Three Kingdoms of England, Scotland and Ireland

activity.notes: The requested 'Kingdoms of Britain' custom-civilization represents the Restoration multiple monarchy rather than a legally united Kingdom of Great Britain, which did not exist until 1707. ATLAS therefore uses the historical composite label 'Three Kingdoms of England, Scotland and Ireland' for Charles II's restored rule from 1660 to 1685. This is a composite political-community label for the three separately constituted kingdoms under one monarch, not a claim that they formed one unitary state. Charles's earlier Scottish kingship of 1649–1651 is not expanded here because this registration represents the Restoration three-kingdom monarchy requested by the mod.

sources.title: Charles II — The National Archives
sources.citation_text: The UK National Archives states that Charles II was King of Scotland in 1649–1651 and King of England, Scotland and Ireland from the Restoration in 1660 until his death in 1685.

sources.title: Restoration — UK Parliament
sources.citation_text: The UK Parliament describes Charles II's formal Restoration to his kingdoms in May 1660 and the continuing separate English and Scottish constitutional context.

sources.title: Britain (Charles II) — Civilization V Customisation Wiki
sources.citation_text: The custom civilization behind the user's label explicitly describes Charles II as ruler of the Three Kingdoms of England, Scotland and Ireland rather than a post-1707 United Kingdom.
